problem:
Consider the following game featuring an unfair coin. If the coin lands on heads, the player wins $$8.$ If the coin lands on tails, the player loses $$2.$ The outcomes of the coin have the following probabilities:

$$
P(\text{Heads})=\frac{1}{4},\,P(\text{Tails})=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

What is the expected profit at each toss in this game?

activity_context.topic_title: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables

feedback.worked_solution:
Let $p$ represent the profit in this game. There are $52$ possible cards that can be selected. One of these cards is the winning card. In the game, there are two possible outcomes:

- If the ace of spades is selected, the player wins $$100.$ This means the player’s profit is $$100-$2=$98,$ so we have $p=98.$

- If the ace of spades is not selected, they lose $$2,$ so we have $p=-2.$

The probabilities for the outcomes are

$$
P(98)=\frac{1}{52},\,P(-2)=\frac{51}{52}.
$$

Let's summarize this in a table. If $p$ is the profit (in dollars) on a single game, and $f(p)$ is the probability mass function for $p,$ then we have the following:

| $p$ | $98$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $f(p)$ | $\frac{1}{52}$ | $\frac{51}{52}$ |

Therefore, the expected value of $p$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[p] & =98\cdot f(98)+(-2)\cdot f(-2) \\  & =98(\frac{1}{52})-2(\frac{51}{52}) \\  & =\frac{98}{52}-\frac{102}{52} \\  & =-\frac{1}{13} \\  & ≈-0.08.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expected profit is approximately $-$\,0.08.$
